title: Counter loop run to escape
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes and distinct states $a$ and $e$. Let $w$ be a Boolean word, and suppose the extra tape initially agrees with the word buffer at cells $cp+p$ for all integers $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$. Given an initial configuration $c$, a run-length function $\\tau$, and an index $r_0$ strictly below the binary value of $w$, suppose each round $r\\le r_0$ starts in state $a$, has positive length, and at every positive intermediate time has a state different from both $a$ and $e$. Suppose also that the configuration after round $r_0$ is in state $e$. If $T$ is the sum of the round lengths for $r\\le r_0$ plus $\\operatorname{overhead}(w,r_0+1)$, then the counter-loop machine reaches its escape configuration at time $T$, with its extra tape on the word cells equal to the counter word after $r_0+1$ decrements. Before $T$ the state is neither done nor escape; through $T$ the extra head lies in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and the first $k$ head positions at each time agree with those of a run of $M$ from some round configuration, either with $r\\le r_0$ and $u\\le\\tau(c_r)$ or with $r=r_0+1$ and $u=0$.
